We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{3}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3} \\ {v}^{′}=16{x}^{3}\, & ⟹\,v=\int 16{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x=4{x}^{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 16{x}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={log}_{3}⁡(x)(4{x}^{4})-\int \frac{4{x}^{4}}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{x}^{4}{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\int 4{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{x}^{4}{log}_{3}⁡(x)-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {x}^{4}+C \\  & =\frac{4{x}^{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}-\frac{{x}^{4}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡x-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}.$
